response:
Diagnosis after gen 6: separating cash-to-price from debt-to-price was the decisive move. CashDebtSplitCleanValue jumped to alpha +0.047 (t = 3.61) with Sharpe 0.379 while keeping FMB 2.98, and the same split structure lifted every quality leg it was paired with — revenue quality (alpha 0.040, t = 3.19, FMB 3.86, Sharpe 0.403), depreciation conservatism (alpha 0.041, t = 2.87, FMB 4.02, coverage 0.136) and taxes payable inside the older net-cash frame (alpha 0.035, t = 2.49). So the mechanism is now clear: equally weighted, separately ranked channels for (i) cash assets per dollar of price, (ii) debt claims per dollar of price, (iii) cross-sectional cheapness and (iv) accounting quality. Two failures also inform this round: CheapWithCashCoverage (alpha −0.023) shows that scaling cash earnings by current liabilities re-introduces a distressed-value tilt, and PayoutWeightedLeveredTrap improved FMB from −0.54 to −1.89 by up-weighting the monotone payout channel, confirming weighting is the active lever. This generation therefore varies weighting and channel composition inside the winning frame, tests a conjunctive (MIN) aggregation, and builds the symmetric trap version to check that the mechanism is two-sided rather than a long-leg artifact.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CashDebtSplitDualQuality
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(dp, at), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Working-capital accruals and depreciation policy measure two independent dimensions of accounting quality — short-term estimate manipulation and long-term conservatism — and cheap, cash-backed firms clean on both are the most reliable value candidates.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Each quality leg separately produced strong results in the split frame (Sloan: alpha 0.047, t = 3.61; depreciation: FMB 4.02, alpha 0.041), and because one is a flow of estimates and the other a policy choice their errors should be largely uncorrelated, so combining them ought to raise the signal-to-noise of the quality dimension. This tests whether quality is one factor or two within the established frame.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashDebtSplitTaxQuality
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(txp, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Earnings that generate a tax liability are externally verified, so tax-confirmed profits are the cheapest available proof that a low-priced firm's income is real rather than accrued.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The tax channel produced alpha 0.035 (t = 2.49) and FMB 3.52 inside the weaker netted-cash frame, so moving it into the split frame that has consistently added roughly one point of alpha t is the natural consolidation test. It also raises coverage to about 0.123 relative to 0.109 because it needs no lagged balance sheet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CashDebtSplitValueQualityBreadth
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(sale, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness confirmed by two independent multiples (book and enterprise-level revenue) and quality confirmed by two independent accrual measures (earnings accruals and revenue collection) is the most robust expression of the cash-backed value idea.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two highest-Sharpe signals in the archive both use the sales-to-EV plus revenue-quality pair, while the two highest-alpha-t signals use book value plus Sloan accruals, and these two pairs disagree on which statistic they maximize. Balancing all four channels against the split cash/debt block tests whether the disagreement reflects noise (in which case both statistics improve) or a genuine trade-off between the two value anchors.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualWeightedCashDebtValue
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: If accounting quality is the binding constraint on whether cheapness pays, it deserves more than an equal share of the composite; doubling its weight should sharpen the separation between genuine value and value traps.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: In the gen-6 winner the accrual screen carried only a quarter of the weight, so we do not yet know whether it is essential or incidental to the +0.047 alpha; this construction gives accruals half the weight and splits the remainder across cash, debt and book value. Comparing the two directly identifies the marginal contribution of the accrual theme, which matters for the economic interpretation of the interaction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: CashBackedCleanValueConjunction
EXPRESSION: MIN(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Balance-sheet strength and cheap-clean accounting are complements: a firm must clear both hurdles, so the weaker of the two composite ranks should determine expected returns rather than their average.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Averaging lets an extreme cash position offset accrual-inflated earnings, which is precisely the substitution the value-trap story says should not be allowed, and the MIN operator enforces the conjunction while leaving both economic channels unchanged. An earlier MIN test was run only inside the HML-loaded book-value family where nothing worked, so this is the first informative test of the aggregation choice within the frame that does work.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: CashPoorLeveredPayoutTrap
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The complete value trap is cash-poor and levered, distributing dividends that exceed accrual-purged cash earnings, with profits sustained by working-capital accruals; such firms should earn reliably negative abnormal returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The trap side has produced large alphas (−0.051 and −0.038) but weak cross-sectional slopes because the skewed net-debt ratio dominated the composite; splitting cash and debt into separate ranks is exactly the fix that repaired the long side, and it is applied here for the first time to the short side. If both FMB and alpha strengthen, the mechanism is symmetric, which materially raises confidence that the long-side result is economic rather than a factor-loading artifact.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
